title: The bug fixers
bridge: A bug fixer works like a careful engineer on a bug: reproduce, write a failing test, fix, watch it pass. Except: the harness runs the before-and-after proof itself, and a failed reproduction is a useful result. A bigger fix waits for a person's Approve.
intro: Bug tickets are the most important trigger. This lesson builds the flow both teams share: triage, reproduce, root cause, smallest fix, proof. Then the FE fixer with browser videos and the BE fixer with a Django test. Last, the flaky-test fixer, which proves 50 green runs in a row.

picture.caption: No fix counts until a test fails without it and passes with it.

steps.text: triage (Sonnet, low): duplicate? right team? how bad?
cannot reproduce: steps tried, data used, what is missing, one question
bigger fix: root cause at file:line and a plan; waits on Approve, Change or Stop
the harness runs the new test on base with only the test files: must fail on behaviour
the same test on the fix: must pass
both logs side by side; the ticket goes to its owner with the PR link

p: Reproduce-first is what makes an agent's bug fix trustworthy. Agentless and SWE-agent are two published research systems that fix GitHub issues with a model. Both work this way.
Triage runs on Sonnet 5.5 at low effort with a structured answer: a duplicate of an open ticket? the right team? how bad? Wrong team: comment and stop.

Reproduction runs on Opus 5.5 at high effort: a failing test, or a recorded browser run on seed data. If it cannot reproduce, it comments on the ticket. The comment lists the steps tried, the seed data and commands used, what is missing, and one specific question. The outcome is handed_off.

Then the plan: the root cause with file:line and why it happened. A fix that is more than a small, local change needs a yes; the agent judges with the fix-bug skill. Its plan goes to the ticket owner with Approve, Change and Stop. The run waits on decidePlan (lesson g5-2) in the same VM.
The fixer looks for the same pattern nearby and lists it in the PR, but fixes only the reported bug. When the PR opens, the ticket is assigned to the routine owner, with the PR link and the proof.

callout.text: A failed reproduction, written up well, is useful on its own. It tells the next person what was tried and what is missing.

sections.h: proveRegressionTest, part 1: base plus the test
p: The proof needs the new test to run twice. First on the base commit with only the test files added: it must fail. Then on the fix: it must pass. If the test passes without the fix, it does not test the bug.
A git worktree is a second checkout of the same repo in another folder, at another commit. The harness makes one at /work/base on the base commit, and copies only the test files into it.
sections.because: A test that never failed proves nothing, so the harness, not the model, shows it failing on the old code.

sections.h: proveRegressionTest, part 2: fail for the right reason
p: The test must fail on behaviour, not on setup. A test that imports a function the fix added fails on base with an ImportError. That proves nothing about the bug, so the fixer rewrites the test until it fails on an assertion.
The Stop hook asks for evidence until both booleans are true. The PR shows both log tails side by side.
sections.because: Failing on an import error is a setup error, not a reproduction, and the proof must tell the two apart.

The bug fixer is not done until both are true.

callout.text: Proof before done. The Stop hook sends the agent back to work until the test has failed on base and passed on the fix.

sections.h: The FE bug fixer: a spec and a video
p: Most FE bugs are visible behaviour. A recorded run that fails before and passes after is proof any reviewer can check in 30 seconds. The FE fixer reproduces on FCP Lab with seed data from TestDataCreator and the e2e apiSetup fixture. Never real data.

Regression specs follow frontend/AGENTS.md: page objects in e2e/pages, test.step with Given, When and Then, assertions on test IDs, ARIA and visible text. A missing locator becomes a page-object method first. Layout bugs are checked at 760 and 1440 wide.

Its charter: frontend/**, six skills (fix-bug, fe-codebase, verify, fcp-lab, pr-story, kb), Opus 5.5 at high. It gets an on-demand VM, not Spot, because it waits on people. The G4 QA agent runs the QA plan in the browser and records the videos. The blank lines are dropped to fit.
sections.because: A short video of the bug and the fix is the proof a reviewer from any team trusts most.

sections.h: The BE bug fixer: a failing Django test first
p: A test that fails on the bug is the cheapest lasting proof in the backend. The BE fixer writes it with CommonRhinoTestCase and the factory_boy factories in rhinoCore/tests/test_factories/models/.

While working, it runs only the affected tests with ./scripts/local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh cloud <label>; before done, the whole module. For an API bug, it adds a curl transcript against FCP Lab, before and after, as text in the PR.

Anything touching the cloud-client gRPC contract, auth or a migration: stop and hand to the BE guild with the reproduction. Its charter is like the FE one, with cloud/**, client/** and sdk/** and migrations denied.
sections.because: A request and response transcript shows a reviewer from the FE side exactly what changed for callers.

code.text:
# cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore/tests/views/test_rh_xxxx_workgroup_list.py: sketch of the failing test the BE bug fixer writes first
"""RH-XXXX (example bug): a member's workgroup list shows a workgroup they don't belong to."""
from rest_framework import status

from rhinoCloud.rhinoCore.tests.test_factories.common_rhino_test_case import CommonRhinoTestCase
from rhinoCloud.rhinoCore.tests.test_factories.models.workgroup_test_factory import WorkgroupTestFactory
from rhinoCloud.rhinoCore.tests.unit_test_utils.list_response import get_uids_from_list_response


class WorkgroupListMembershipRegressionTestCase(CommonRhinoTestCase):
    def test_member_sees_only_their_own_workgroups(self):
        unrelated = WorkgroupTestFactory()  # fake data from the factories only

        response = self.primary_member_client.get("/api/v2/workgroups/")

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, status.HTTP_200_OK)
        listed = get_uids_from_list_response(response)
        self.assertIn(str(self.primary_workgroup.uid), listed)
        self.assertNotIn(str(unrelated.uid), listed)  # fails on main, passes with the fix


# While working: ./scripts/local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh cloud rhinoCloud.rhinoCore.tests.views.test_rh_xxxx_workgroup_list

p: The nightly run is green 5 times out of 20. Flaky tests teach people and agents to ignore red. FlakyGuard is a flaky-test repair system that Uber published. It repaired about half of the flaky tests it could reproduce.

The trigger is a Jira ticket labelled flaky-test, filed by G7's nightly triage and picked up by the G5-13 poller. One run per test (flaky:fcp:<hash of the test id>), 1 slot. Only tests that run in the VM; tests that need the QA environments go back to the BE guild.

It reproduces first: the test's whole module with Django's --shuffle and a new seed each time, until it fails. A seed is the number that fixes a random order, so the same seed gives the same order. No failure in 200 runs: hand back with the seeds tried.

Done: the root cause in one line with file:line, and 50 green runs in a row with the old failing seed. Its charter never allows add_retries_or_sleeps or edit_test_assertions. The blank lines are dropped to fit.
sections.because: A retry or a sleep hides a flake; only finding the cause, and 50 green runs, shows it is gone.

lab.title: Judge three bug fixes (reading lab)

worked.do: A new test imports formatQuota, a helper the fix added. On base it fails with ImportError. What does RegressionProof say?
worked.see: failsWithoutFix is false (isSetupError). The fixer rewrites the test so it fails on behaviour, for example by asserting on the rendered text.

worked.do: A new test passes on base and on the fix. Is the bug reproduced?
worked.see: No. failsWithoutFix is false: the test does not catch the bug, so it proves nothing.

worked.do: The FE fixer cannot reproduce an RH bug after trying three paths. What goes on the ticket?
worked.see: The steps tried, the seed data and commands, what is missing (role, data shape, browser, exact steps) and one specific question. Outcome handed_off.

worked.do: The root cause is in a shared serializer used by four views. Does the run wait?
worked.see: Yes: more than a small, local change. The plan goes to the ticket owner with Approve, Change and Stop, and the run waits on decidePlan.

worked.do: The flaky fixer's proveStable fails at run 37 with seed 5036. What does the PR need now?
worked.see: Nothing yet: ok is false, greenInARow 36. The fixer keeps looking for the cause; done needs 50 of 50.

worked.do: The flaky fixer adds time.sleep(1) and gets 50 green runs. Is it done?
worked.see: No. add_retries_or_sleeps is in its never-list, so the false-heal check rejects the run (lesson g5-5).

lab.faded: Write the ticket comment for a BE bug the fixer could not reproduce. The bug: a member sometimes sees another workgroup's dataset. List three steps tried and the data used. The one specific question at the end is left to you.
lab.alone: Write a Playwright regression spec in the same style for a made-up bug: "the empty projects table shows no message". Use Given, When and Then steps, seed data through apiSetup, and assert on visible text. Say which line fails on main.
lab.done: Given a test and two runs, you can say whether it reproduces the bug. You can say why a sleep is never a fix.

quiz.q: Who runs the new test on the base commit, and why?

options.text: The harness, in a worktree with only the test files added, so the failure is evidence the model did not produce
options.why: The proof must not depend on the agent's word.

options.text: The agent, so it can fix the test if it fails
options.why: The agent may rewrite a test that fails on setup, but the proof run is the harness's.
The proof is part of done, before any PR.

quiz.q: The bug fixer cannot reproduce the bug. What is the right outcome?

options.text: Guess a fix from the description and open a draft
options.why: Reproduce-first is the rule. A guess is not trustworthy.

options.text: A ticket comment with what was tried, what is missing and one question; outcome handed_off
options.why: A failed reproduction, written up well, is useful on its own.

options.text: Retry the reproduction until it works
options.why: There is no point retrying blind; a person can add the missing detail.

quiz.q: How does the flaky-test fixer prove a fix?

options.text: 50 green runs in a row with new seeds, including the seed that used to fail
options.why: proveStable runs 50 seeds; the PR shows 50/50 and the old failing seed.
A flaky test is green most of the time anyway.
Retries and sleeps are false heals for this routine.

words.plain: The rule that a bug fixer shows the bug before it changes any code.
A test that fails on the bug and passes on the fix, so the bug cannot come back silently.
A second checkout of the same repo in another folder, at another commit.
A test failure caused by loading or imports, not by behaviour; it does not count as a reproduction.
The number that fixes a random order, so the same seed gives the same test order.
A test that sometimes passes and sometimes fails on the same code.
